findings:
🟠 [panel-finish-rebudget] MUST-FIX In `performFinalPanel`'s batch path the second `performReview({ preparedLaunch, providedReviewResult })` call does not forward `prepared_review`, so it re-runs `prepareReview` (second diff mkdtemp + packet build per seat) and re-evaluates `campaignWallBudgetStatus`/`campaignWallRemainingSeconds` with a post-batch `this.now()`; because each seat's `--timeout` and helper `timeout_seconds` equal the whole panel remainder, a batch whose slowest seat runs to its cap finishes with elapsed ≥ limit, and every seat (including ones that returned a valid verdict) is discarded as `phase: 'campaign_wall_budget'` instead of being finished. No test reaches this path (all engine tests inject a stub dispatcher, so `injectedDispatcher` forces the sequential seam, and `seqDigest` is never compared). Smallest fix: when `preparedLaunch` is set, skip `prepareReview` and the budget/clamp block (carry `prepared_review`/`reviewTimeoutSeconds` from the deferred return) and go straight to `reviewTask`; add one engine case with the default dispatcher and a stub `scriptPath` that asserts receipts/`review_digest` equal the sequential run.
🟠 [reserve-not-sealed] MUST-FIX `src/engine/campaign-intake.js` (+ mirror) is untouched, so `final_panel_reserve_seconds` and `full_suite_reuse` are never sealed into `initial_state.limits`; the engine falls back to `control.contract`, which is not part of the sealed state, so a resumed campaign whose control carries only `initial_state` reads reserve 0 and refuses the panel (`final_panel_budget_exhausted`), and the acceptance row `pocket` ("capped identically at ... intake") has no intake layer. Fix: seal both into `initial_state.limits` at intake (defaults 0 / true, 0..1800 check) and read only `initial_state.limits` in the two budget helpers and the `fullSuite` knob.
🟡 [acceptance-gate-ignores-wall] MUST-FIX The convergence gate change sets `passed = gate.verdict === 'PASS'` and only applies `budget.exhausted` when `reason !== 'acceptance'`, so the acceptance gate now passes even when wall and pocket are both exhausted; the spec's rule is one consumer-scoped remainder, not an exemption. Fix: keep `passed = !budget.exhausted && gate.verdict === 'PASS'` with `{ consumer: reason === 'acceptance' ? 'panel' : 'review' }`.
🟡 [batch-identity-weak] MUST-FIX Acceptance `batch-identity` requires field-by-field identity of result JSON, envelope and packet fields; the added test compares only `status`, `signal`, `result.verdict`, `result.status`. Fix: `assert.deepStrictEqual(batch, single)` on the full objects (same fixture, same stub), which the shared code path should satisfy.
🔵 [test-debug-leftovers] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The engine test writes `/tmp/flag-debug.json` / `/tmp/red-debug.json` on failure and carries `void first; void refused;`; cosmetic, excluded because it does not affect correctness.
🔵 [inherit-stdio-buffered] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `dispatchReview` with `stdio: 'inherit'` now buffers child output through the helper (1 MiB cap) and replays it after exit instead of streaming; acceptable under the single-launch-path rule, noted only so callers that watched live output are not surprised.
